title: Capacity & Price-Shock Protocol and Hiring Hooks
content:
Purpose:
This is a working protocol to guide finance + hiring decisions in the event of abrupt pricing pressure (market rate compression or competitive token price drops) or demand surges. It combines a compact sensitivity framework with discrete hiring triggers and prioritized countermeasures to preserve runway and SLAs.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Build 3 actionable scenarios (mild, medium, severe) capturing price-per-token compression and regional spot-GPU cost inflation;
- Link each scenario to explicit headcount triggers (by role and tenure) and spend-reduction levers;
- Define a small, fast checklist of immediate steps for first 72 hours and 30-day follow-ups;
- Keep runway-impact banding and a conservative reserve bucket (10% of Opex) for capacity hedges.

Assumptions (baseline model inputs):
- ARR mix: 62% hosted API, 25% Dedicated, 13% Private.
- Token mix: 70% generation, 20% embeddings, 10% reranking; average price-per-thousand-tokens = $0.45 baseline.
- GPU cost baseline: $0.65/token-equivalent for serving (includes infra, ops, licensing amortization).
- Current headcount (finance-enabled roles): 148 FTEs; hiring pipeline active for 18 roles over 6 months.

Scenarios (high-level):
1) Mild compression: price-per-token -10%, demand flat.
   Impact: revenue -6% (mix effects), unit margin -4pp.
   HC triggers: pause non-critical external hires; defer 25% of contractor spend.
2) Moderate shock: price-per-token -25% + 8% demand growth (price elasticity).
   Impact: revenue -15% net, unit margin -10pp, short-term pressure on Dedicated yield.
   HC triggers: pause all non-essential hires; freeze promotions >10% comp unless strategic; convert 3 planned infra hires to contractors.
3) Severe price shock + regional cost spike: price-per-token -40% while spot GPU costs +35% in APAC region.
   Impact: revenue -28%, gross margin compresses by ~20pp, potential 6–9 month runway cut.
   HC triggers: immediate hiring freeze; enact 8% headcount reduction as phased layoffs (priority to open roles, contractors first).

Hiring hook definitions (how we translate signals into actions):
- Trigger 1 (early warning): Two consecutive weeks of ARR bookings below expected by >5% and price index down >=10% -> implement hiring pause on non-customer-facing roles within 7 days.
- Trigger 2 (escalation): Monthly revenue decline >12% or gross margin <target -12pp -> move to targeted role reductions and budget reallocation.
- Trigger 3 (critical): Runway <6 months at burn rate -> execute contingency headcount reductions and escalate to exec council for pricing changes.

Prioritized mitigation levers (ranked):
1) Price-side: temporary token floor for new customers, targeted uplift on enterprise contracts, short-term promo removal;
2) Cost-side: tighten batch sizing and caching thresholds (ops); reduce autoscaling headroom for non-critical routes; ramp compressing quantized model variants for low tier;
3) Capacity hedges: shift non-latency workloads to cheaper regions temporarily, activate reserved GPU pools, reduce long-lived burst capacity;
4) People levers: hiring freeze, contractor re-eval, selective role consolidation.

Quick 72-hour checklist (operational):
- Finance run: re-run cash flow with scenario weights and updated pricing assumptions (owner: Marcus)
- Sales: immediate pause on promotional credits; review upcoming renewals for uplift (owner: Sofia)
- Product/Serving: toggle less expensive model variants for 10% of traffic, adjust autoscale windows (owner: Gabe)
- Legal/Commercial: prepare amendment template for adjusting new customers' price tiers (owner: Elena)

30-day plan:
- Finalize headcount decision tree and internal comms; publish required HR timeline;
- Execute 30-day capacity rebalancing (region shifts + reserved capacity activation);
- Test customer communication scripts and a 2-week A/B on token floor adjustments for new signups.

Metrics to monitor (daily/weekly):
- Token price index, realized per-token revenue, gross margin per route, committed capacity vs. reserved, net new MRR, contractor spend by team.

Unresolved questions / open items:
- Appetite for temporary, low-latency SLA relaxations for non-premium customers?
- Legal constraints on contractual price floors for existing enterprise deals (need legal signoff).
- Runbook for dedicated customers who require exact capacity; who authorizes region swap?

Next steps / owners:
- Build a compact spreadsheet model (sheet id in linked artifacts) with toggles for token price, GPU cost, and hiring actions (owner: Marcus) – due EOD +3 days.
- Draft comms templates and escalation ladder (owner: Elena) – due EOD +5 days.
- Ops playbook to flip model variants and limit auto-burst (owner: Gabe) – due +7 days.

Notes: This is a working doc — granular numbers in the linked sheet. The intention is to keep the decision path short and the actions reversible where possible. Feedback welcome; flag any missing role categories that should be explicitly protected or reprioritized.
